interest: This file provides an intriguing glimpse into the ceremonial protocol and sartorial expectations of the Japanese Imperial Court during the early Showa era as documented by the U.S. Department of State. It illustrates how private American citizens directly consulted the State Department regarding social and diplomatic etiquette for presentations before foreign royalty. Additionally, it preserves concrete details of court attire regulations, notably the distinction between afternoon dress for private audiences (with a prohibition on black) and formal evening dress featuring a four-yard shoulder train for state functions like the Imperial New Year's Reception.
keywords: Division of International Conferences and Protocol
overview: This file comprises correspondence from November and December 1930 between Miss Rosalind Gluck of Minneapolis, Minnesota, and the Department of State concerning the dress regulations for American women presented at the Imperial Court of Japan. Miss Gluck inquired about appropriate attire and specific rules regarding dress and train lengths. In response, Richard Southgate, Assistant Chief of the Division of International Conferences and Protocol, advised on behalf of the Secretary of State that private audiences required standard afternoon dress (avoiding black), whereas formal occasions such as the New Year's Reception mandated evening wear with a four-yard train suspended from the shoulders.

subfiles.summary: Miss Rosalind Gluck of Minneapolis writes to the Secretary of State inquiring where to obtain information on the type of dress worn by American women when presented at the Japanese Court. She specifically requests details regarding the prescribed length of both the gown and the train. The document bears official Department of State filing and acknowledgement stamps dating from late November and early December 1930.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rosalind Gluck to Secretary of State regarding Japanese Court dress regulations

subfiles.about: Official reply detailing the attire and four-yard train requirements for foreign women attending private audiences and formal receptions at the Japanese Court.
subfiles.from: Richard Southgate (Assistant Chief, Division of International Conferences and Protocol)
subfiles.summary: Writing on behalf of the Secretary of State, Assistant Chief Richard Southgate replies to Rosalind Gluck's inquiry regarding court attire in Japan. He explains that for private audiences, foreign and American women wear customary afternoon dress, strictly avoiding black. For formal state events such as the New Year's Reception, evening dress is required with a shoulder train whose official regulation length was established as four yards.
